fact_text: The FY26 federal budget was presented by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb and followed by a post-budget press conference where FBR officials were questioned on enforcement.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: The FY26 budget set the fiscal deficit at about 5 trillion rupees, or 3.9% of GDP, which a guest called one of the lowest deficit ratios since 2003.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest cited the Economic Survey as showing agriculture output shrinking in FY25, with livestock the largest part of the sector and hard to measure, so it is reported in a way that hides the decline.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest said manufacturing also fell in FY25, and that World Bank reporting showed rising unemployment and poverty, so he did not see the year as good for Pakistan.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: The FY26 budget cut the salary tax rate for lower earners, but the cut stopped at incomes of about 1 to 1.5 lakh rupees, so relief for salaried people with an effective rate of 23-24% was small.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest estimated the monthly gain from FY26 salary tax changes at roughly 500 to 7,500 rupees, depending on income band.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest said the salary tax base of 6 lakh rupees was left unchanged and was wrong in principle, noting that India's equivalent threshold is about 36 lakh rupees.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest said the top salary tax rate is about 38.5%, and that with corporate and dividend taxes the total burden on a business can reach around 60%.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest said high salary taxation is driving qualified professionals out of Pakistan, a brain drain the FY26 budget did not address.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: The FY26 budget introduced a digital services tax, which a guest compared with India's 2016 equalisation levy, and said it would not be a large revenue source.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A proposed law would bar non-filers, those not registered for income tax or sales tax, from opening bank accounts, buying property or buying a car; it had stalled in the assembly for about six months.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest warned that a widened definition of tax fraud could let an income tax officer arrest a person, who must then appear before a magistrate within 24 hours, and urged that this power be removed or qualified.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A former FBR chairman said the Taj scheme, which relied on voluntary registration, was discontinued, so making registration compulsory through enforcement would not work.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: The FBR tax revenue target for FY26 was cited as 14.1 trillion rupees, about 2.1 to 2.2 trillion above the FY25 level, of which roughly 1.3 to 1.4 trillion was organic growth.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A former FBR chairman estimated the FY26 revenue gap at 450 to 500 billion rupees, after about 350 to 400 billion from new measures against an 800 to 900 billion rise in revenue.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: FBR said enforcement raised about 50 billion rupees in FY25, which a guest said it had shown the IMF as a basis for expecting similar enforcement gains in FY26.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest said the government's stated choice was between enforcement and higher taxes, and that it named no retail-sector steps in the budget itself.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest said FBR already holds lifestyle data on vehicles, houses and travel, and that political will would be enough to use it for taxing people with visible wealth.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: The FY26 petroleum development levy was budgeted at 1.5 trillion rupees, which a guest said would be met with 3% volume growth even at a 77 rupee rate.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: The FY26 budget cut the super tax by 0.5 percentage point on income of 20 to 50 crore rupees, so a 2% rate fell to 1.5% and a 1.5% rate fell to 1%.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: The FY26 finance minister described the super tax cut and the salary relief as a journey, promising further reductions in later budgets; the guest said the tax base had not been broadened.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: Mutual fund dividends are taxed at 25% where at least 50% of fund income is from debt, and at 15% where it comes mainly from equity, a split introduced in FY25.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest said the FY26 mutual fund dividend wording changed but the rate for money market and income funds stayed at 25%, while balanced funds could face proportional 15% and 25% rates.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest cited withholding on profit on bank deposits at 15 to 20% and said investors weigh principal protection more than tax, so the budget was unlikely to shift money to stocks in the short term.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest said provincial agricultural income tax projections, such as Punjab's of about 4 to 5 billion rupees, are too small to matter, and that middlemen's profits, which raise food prices, remain untaxed.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest said agricultural income tax is a provincial subject while middlemen (aratis) are a federal matter, so the tax cannot be reached by provincial action alone.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest said the IMF programme leaves little fiscal space, so the budget could not broaden taxes on documented retail and wholesale sectors and had to rely on enforcement.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest rated the FY26 budget overall good for fiscal consolidation and for avoiding new burdens on documented sectors, while the enforcement power was seen as open to abuse.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest said the electric vehicle policy was announced ahead of the budget but was still not issued, so the carbon levy on petrol vehicles came before the promised EV incentives and home-charging tariff.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: The FY26 budget raised the sales tax on small cars from 12.5% to 18%, and set petrol, diesel and hybrid vehicles that paid under 18% at 18%.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: The FY26 budget introduced a carbon levy on internal combustion vehicles, charged in slabs by engine power, with the stated aim of discouraging polluting cars and cutting fuel import costs.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest said the budget did not lift the age limit on imported five-year-old used cars, which removed a threat to locally assembled cars and gave assemblers a breathing space.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest cited about 50% of the price of locally assembled cars as taxes, and said new entrants and imports had increased competition after the earlier policy change.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest said Chinese, South Korean and French models entering the market after the new policy showed that more imports would push local car prices down once the import age limit is raised.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest said the refinery upgrade needs investment of about 5 to 6 billion dollars, and that the budget did not resolve the sales tax and inland freight equalisation margin issues needed to unlock it.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: Refinery policy was first issued in August 2023, a related issue was resolved in February 2024, and the one-year backlog was to be handled through the inland freight equalisation margin rather than the budget.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest said the budget gave steel and cement sectors clearer tax treatment, and that cement would benefit if the real estate sector revives.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: The FY26 budget removed the 7% federal excise duty on houses, plots and commercial property, a levy that had been applied earlier.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: The FY26 budget proposed cutting Islamabad property stamp duty from 4% to 1%, and a tax credit for flats up to 2,000 square feet.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: For property above 50 million rupees, the budget moved 1.5 points of tax from buyer to seller, so total transaction cost stayed about 6 to 8%, a guest said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: The budget defined an eligible filer for property purchases above a threshold by cash and cashable resources in the wealth statement, which a guest called impractical for an official to assess.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest said transfer taxes are about 16% for filers and 40% for non-filers, so a 100 million rupee property would cost 16 million for filers and 40 million for non-filers.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest said about 52% of Karachi's population lives in slums, katchi abadis or unapproved buildings, and that the filer concept took about 20 years to be widely understood.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest cited a housing shortage of about 12 million homes in Pakistan and said the construction chain links about 72 industries and 10 million workers.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest said overseas Pakistanis remitted about 38 billion dollars in FY25 and that about 52% of those remittances went into real estate and construction.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A developer said about 100 fifty-storey projects are ready in one Karachi district, each with a sales value of 75 to 100 million dollars, a pipeline of about 5 billion dollars.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest said plots above 120 gaz must by law be auctioned by the Board of Revenue, but auctions did not happen for decades, and that the supply block keeps prices high.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest said releasing land and extending infrastructure to the outskirts could correct property prices by about 50%.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest said banks have historically asked for a 40% down payment, and suggested 10 to 15% down with instalments for the rest as a route to home ownership.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A guest said a person earning 2 million rupees a year cannot buy a 50 million rupee house after tax and living costs, so the middle-class market is largely unaffordable.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A developer said housing tax formulas changed several times in five to six years, so a project from land to completion cannot be planned, and that 10 to 15 years of legislated policy is needed.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A developer said several years of pressure on the property business had lowered buyer confidence, so builders will not start projects without buyers.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)

fact_text: A manufacturer said his factory operating since 1960 runs at about 35% of capacity because of weak offtake, and that his plant is debt-free.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Good or Bad? Post-budget Analysis for Fiscal Year 2025-26 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-11)
